messages:
jordan: Heads-up — seeing a burst of 403s for embeddings calls after the KMS rewrap job yesterday. started ~10:23 UTC. sample log below, can someone triage?

maria: oh — which route specifically? embeddings-only or a shared route?

jordan: embeddings route /v1/embeddings. key_tag in the metadata changed during rewrap. log snippet: 
```
2026-03-19T10:23:11Z request_id=abc123 route=/v1/embeddings token_id=svc-emu-42 status=403 reason="scope_mismatch" scope_expected="embeddings:write" scope_present="chat:write"
kms.key_tag=key-2026-03-19-rewrap-7 token.tag=tag-OLD
```

jordan: repro curl: 
```
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -d '{"input":"x"}'
# -> 403 scope_mismatch
```

simon: hmm. remember the recent RBAC refactor that moved primary scope resolution from token metadata to route-level allowlist lookups? if the KMS rewrap dropped or mutated the token tag that maps to scopes, the allowlist check would fail. could be cache eviction timing + rewrap.

maria: @simon do we have a short-term mitigation? we should avoid customer impact. can we temporarily fall back to metadata-based checks while we root cause.

simon: short term: enable authz fallback (feature_flag.authz_fallback=true) at the edge to skip strict route-allowlist enforcement and accept legacy token tags. also flush the scope cache for suspected tokens: `POST /admin/cache/flush?prefix=scope:`

devops-bot: deploy triggered by simon: authz-fallback flag set in namespace prod-edge at 10:46 UTC — rollout 3/3.

jordan: did that reduce the error volume?

maria: yes, errors dropped back to baseline after the flag and cache flush. but audit shows some tokens had both chat and embeddings scopes before the rewrap; after rewrap the token_tag field was missing for a subset. that suggests KMS metadata sync lost token_tag on re-encrypt.

security-bot: created ticket INC-2026-237 to track root cause + audit timeline. assigned to @simon. severity=P2.

simon: next steps I'm taking: 1) reproduce the rewrap locally with our metadata pipeline, 2) add a guard in token-service so rewrap preserves scope-related tags, 3) add extra fields to authz-failure audit logs (include key_tag and token_tag) for easier forensics.

jordan: can we also scan for per-route allowlists that reference transient tags? if a token tag is ephemeral we should never rely on it. might be a policy smell.

maria: running an audit query now: `select token_id, last_rewrap, scope_tags from key_metadata where last_rewrap > '2026-03-19T00:00:00Z'` — will paste results in the ticket.

jordan: good. if this touches customers we'll draft a short incident note. :+1:

simon: small protective PR up to ensure tag preservation: https://git.internal/r/redwood/token-service/pulls/342 — adds e2e test for rewrap metadata retention.

maria: ack. I'll update INC-2026-237 with the audit dump and timeline.

jordan: once simon validates the fix in staging we'll revert the authz-fallback flag and re-enable strict enforcement. keep me posted if anything new pops up.
